questions.stem: By considering mass defect, calculate the kinetic energy of the alpha particle, and explain why it is significantly greater than that of the polonium atom.
questions.stimulus: A radon-198 atom, initially at rest, undergoes alpha decay. The masses of the atoms involved are shown in atomic mass units (u). [Equation: radon-198 → polonium-194 + helium-4, with masses 197.999 u, 193.988 u and 4.00260 u.] The kinetic energy of the polonium atom produced is 2.55 × 10−14 J.

criteria.text: Applies correct method to calculate KE of the alpha particle ; Explains the greater KE of the alpha particle using the principle of conservation of momentum
Applies correct method to calculate KE of the alpha particle ; Applies the principle of conservation of momentum
Shows the main steps of the calculation of KE ; Shows a sound understanding of the conservation of momentum
Shows step(s) of the calculation of KE ; Shows some understanding of the conservation of momentum
Provides some relevant information

answersCouldInclude: Calculation not using mass defect (K → P).
questions.sampleAnswerTruncated:
Alpha decay
Mass defect = 197.999 – (193.988 + 4.000260) = 0.0084u
Converting to kilograms = 0.0084 × 1.661 × 10–27 = 1.395 × 10–29 kg
Total energy produced = mc2 = 1.395 × 10–29 × (3 × 108)2 = 1.256 × 10–12 J
KEalpha = Total Energy produced – KEpolonium = 1.256 × 10–12 – 2.44 × 10–14
= 1.23 × 10–12 J
Since the radon atom is initially at rest, the decay products move away from each other with equal and opposite momenta. As the alpha particle’s mass is significantly less than that of the polonium atom, it therefore has a significantly higher velocity (p = mv), and consequently a higher KE.
